content: 1. Phenytoin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It also decreases their levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. If estrogens are used for contraception, contraceptive failure may occur. 2. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 3. Prednisone reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 4. Pretomanid increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens through inhibition of OAT3 transporters. In vitro studies show significant OAT3 inhibition. Monitor for increased adverse effects and consider dosage reduction for OAT3 substrates. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 5. Primidone reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 6. Quercetin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 7. Quinupristin/dalfopristin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. Quinupristin/dalfopristin also increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 8. Ranolazine increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 9. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 11. Rifapentine reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 12. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 13. Roxithromycin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 14. Rufinamide reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Simvastatin increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 16. Sirolimus increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 17. Oral estrogens may reduce the serum IGF-1 response to somapacitan, potentially requiring higher somapacitan dosages. Refer to the drug monograph for starting dose recommendations. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 18. St. John’s Wort reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 19. Stiripentol affects hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP1A2 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects, and adjust dosages as needed. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Streptomycin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 21. Sulfadiazine reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 22. Sulfamethoxazole reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 23. Sulfisoxazole reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 24. Tacrolimus increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 25. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Tecovirimat reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered. Use caution and monitor. 27. Teicoplanin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 28. Temocillin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 29. Tenapanor reduces the levels of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting the intestinal uptake transporter OATP2B1, which may reduce the exposure of OATP2B1 substrates. Use caution and monitor. 30. Teniposide increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 31. Tesamorelin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering metabolism. This may decrease efficacy; monitor closely. 32. Tetracycline reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 33. Tigecycline reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 34. Tobramycin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 35. Tolvaptan increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 36. Topiramate reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 37. Trazodone reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 38. Trimethoprim reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 39. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels or effects of ubrogepant by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustment is recommended when ubrogepant is used with moderate or weak CYP3A4 inducers. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Vadadustat increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by increasing exposure of OAT3 substrates. Monitor for signs of adverse effects of OAT3 substrates and reduce substrate doses as per product labeling. Use caution and monitor. 41. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels or effects of valproic acid by increasing its elimination, which may lead to increased seizure frequency. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Vancomycin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of hormones and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 43. Verapamil increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 44. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 45. Zafirlukast increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 46. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 47. Conjugated estrogens may interact with tricyclic antidepressants (e.g., amitriptyline, amoxapine, clomipramine, desipramine, dosulepin, doxepin, imipramine, lofepramine, nortriptyline, protriptyline, and maprotiline) by an unspecified mechanism. Estrogens and progestins may decrease antidepressant effects while increasing plasma concentrations and adverse effects of tricyclic antidepressants. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 48. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels of ascorbic acid by increasing its elimination. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 49. Boron increases the levels of conjugated estrogens by altering their metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 50. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels of cyanocobalamin (vitamin B12) by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 51. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 52. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels of L-methylfolate by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 53. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 54. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels of magnesium salts (e.g., magnesium chloride, citrate, hydroxide, oxide, and sulfate) by shifting magnesium from blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 55. Conjugated estrogens reduce the effects of metyrapone by an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 56. Mycophenolate reduces the effects of conjugated estrogens by an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance is unclear. 57. Phytoestrogens reduce the effects of conjugated estrogens through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 58. Pleurisy root reduces the effects of conjugated estrogens by an unspecified mechanism. This is a theoretical interaction, and the clinical significance is minor or unknown. 59. Natural progesterone and conjugated estrogens may interact through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially causing breast tenderness. The clinical significance is minor or unknown. 60. Conjugated estrogens reduce the levels of pyridoxine (vitamin B6) by altering its metabolism. The clinical significance is minor or unknown.
